To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a nine amino acid sequence located at the C‐termini of the Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 sodium channels contains sufficient information to direct axonal compartmentalisation of proteins and that the axonal compartmentalized proteins are eliminated from the dendrites by endocytotic mechanisms.
the C‐termini of neuronal sodium channels contain axonal targeting information and that the axonal compartmentalized sodium channel Nav1 is recognized by the endocytic pathway in hippocampal neurons.

the C‐terminal region (CT) of neuronal sodium channels contains information that targets the protein to axons, and that a nine amino acid sequence within the CT of sodium channels is recognized by the endocytic machinery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of axonal determinants in the cytoplasmatic C‐terminal domain of neuronal sodium channel.
the mechanisms that regulate the distribution of proteins in axons and dendrites.
the identification of a novel mechanism that regulates the selective distribution of a protein to axons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
axonal targeting is mediated by the C‐terminal region and that the di‐leucline‐based motif mediating the axonal compartmentalized distribution is located within a nine amino acid sequence.
Nav1.2 contains a C‐terminal region with a di‐leukine motif, which is necessary and sufficient for axonal targeting and endocytosis.
the di‐leu‐cine‐containing C‐terminus region of Nav1 is a determinant for axonal compartment‐alization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C‐terminal region, especially the nine amino acid segment containing the di‐leuine motif of sodium channel, plays an important role in targeting the sodium channel protein to the axon.
we have identified a di‐leuine‐based motif in the sodium channel Nav 1.2 C terminus that is necessary and sufficient for axonal targeting of a reporter protein.
a short region of Nav1.C‐terminus is a sufficient determinant for the selective targeting of proteins to axons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axonal targeting signal in the C‐terminal region is sufficient to target proteins to axon and that this signal is mediated by the clathin pathway.
the C‐terminal region containing di‐leucines in Nav1.2 sodium channel is sufficient to target the protein to axons and that this targeting may be mediated by endocytotic mechanisms.
a di‐leucline motif within a C‐terminal domain of the neuronal sodium channel Nav 1.2 is sufficient to target a reporter protein to axonal compartments.
